title: Dos Pronombres Juntos — Practice
description: Authored B1 practice set for double object pronouns: indirect before direct (me lo, te la), le/les becoming se before lo/la, and where the pair goes with commands, infinitives and gerunds.

lessons.summary: When both pronouns show up, the order is fixed: INDIRECT first, DIRECT second — me lo, te la, nos los. '¿Me pasas el babero?' → '¿Me lo pasas?'. The famous twist: le and les turn into SE before lo/la/los/las — 'Le doy el chupete' → 'Se lo doy' (never «le lo»). Spanish simply refuses two l-pronouns in a row. Since se could be him, her, them or usted, add an a-phrase when it matters: 'Se lo di a la maestra'. Placement mirrors single pronouns, but the pair never splits: before a conjugated verb ('Te lo preparo ahora'), attached to an affirmative command ('Dámelo', 'Pásamela'), before a negative one ('No se lo des'), and with an infinitive or gerund you choose — both attached ('Voy a dárselo', accent added) or both in front ('Se lo voy a dar') — never one on each side.

examples.english: The bib? I'll pass it to you now.

examples.spanish: ¿El chupete? Se lo doy antes de dormir.
examples.english: The dummy? I give it to him before sleep.

examples.spanish: Ese es mi libro — dámelo, porfa.
examples.english: That's my book — give it to me, please.

examples.spanish: Es su juguete favorito, no se lo quites.
examples.english: It's his favourite toy, don't take it from him.

examples.spanish: Se la voy a leer esta noche. / Voy a leérsela esta noche.
examples.english: I'm going to read it to her tonight.
examples.note: both in front, or both attached — never split

items.promptEnglish: —Can you pass me the bib? —Yes, I'll pass it to you now.
items.explanation: Indirect first, direct second: te (to you) + lo (the bib).

items.promptEnglish: The dummy? I only give it to him for sleeping.
items.explanation: Le + lo is forbidden — le becomes se before lo/la: se lo doy.

items.promptEnglish: —And my mug? —I'll bring it to you right away.
items.explanation: La taza is feminine → la; the person first: te la traigo (or se la, speaking to usted).

items.promptEnglish: That's daddy's — give it to me, please.
items.explanation: With an affirmative command both pronouns attach, in me-lo order: dá-me-lo.

items.prompt: Todavía no puede comer eso — no ___ des.
items.promptEnglish: He can't eat that yet — don't give it to him.
items.explanation: Negative command: pronouns in front, and le → se before lo: no se lo des.

items.promptEnglish: The story? I'm going to read it to him tonight.
items.explanation: The pair stays together: both before (se lo voy a leer) or both attached (voy a leérselo) — never one each side.

items.prompt: ¿Las fotos del bebé? ___ ___ mando a los abuelos hoy. (dos pronombres)
items.promptEnglish: The baby photos? I'll send them to the grandparents today.
items.explanation: Les (a los abuelos) → se before las (las fotos): se las mando.

items.prompt: «Se lo di ___.» — ¿cómo aclaras que fue a la maestra?
items.promptEnglish: "I gave it to her." — how do you clarify it was the teacher?
items.explanation: Se is ambiguous, so you clarify with an a-phrase: se lo di a la maestra.

items.promptEnglish: The ball, pass it to me — it's my turn!
items.explanation: Attached to the command in me-la order: pása-me-la. «Pásalame» scrambles the order.

items.promptEnglish: —The milk? —I'm making it for him right now.
items.explanation: Attached to the gerund as one word: preparándosela (se for him, la for la leche).

items.prompt: —¿Quién les regaló esos juguetes? —___ regalaron los tíos.
items.promptEnglish: —Who gave you (all) those toys? —The aunt and uncle gave them to us.
items.explanation: Nos (to us) before los (the toys): nos los regalaron.
Le → se before lo, and indirect goes first: se lo expliqué.
